Test Lab · Composite v2 research · 17 Jul 2026

Qwen-Image-Edit-2511: iterative character insertion on a real watercolor plate

Model alibaba:qwen-image-edit@2511 via our existing Runware account. Scene = production empty scene (pirate story P1, staging). Characters = the exact styled-avatar reference photos the pipeline feeds Grok. Two sequential insertions, $0.008 per call, $0.016 total.

Verdict: structurally, the background holds. Across both insertions nothing moved — swing, bench, fence, picnic table and path all stay put; the changes near the figures are legitimate occlusion. What it is not is pixel-exact: each call re-renders the full frame with a faint global tone/edge shift (the thin red outlines in the heatmaps). For a hard guarantee, gate the output through the SAM figure mask — see below.

Scale: 0 = identical, 255 = maximal change, mean over greyscale pixels. The ~6–8 floor in untouched regions is the global re-render shift (tone + resampling) — visible as thin outlines, not moved objects.

What this means for the pipeline

  • One person at a time — yes. The model takes max 3 input images per call, so multi-character pages build iteratively. No manual final composite: every call returns the fully integrated frame.
  • Background: structurally untouched, not pixel-untouched. For the moving-table guarantee, composite the model output back onto the previous frame only inside the new figure's dilated SAM mask (the same silhouette-gated paste char repair already uses). Then the table physically cannot move — the model only owns the small tolerance band around the figure — and cumulative tone drift over 4+ insertions dies too.
  • Cost: $0.008/call at this resolution → a 4-character page ≈ $0.03, cheaper than one Grok page today.
  • Open before trusting it: identity scores vs refs (run our eval on these), 4-insertion drift, interacting poses (hug / hand-holding across separate calls), and whether occlusion order is steerable (Hans landed in front of the bench — right here, but must be controllable).

Round 2 — the realistic case: seated interaction with scene objects

Same plate, same refs, harder ask: the boy must SIT on the swing, the man must SIT on the bench — pose synthesis + object contact + occlusion in both directions. $0.018 for both calls.

Round 3 — 4 characters, full-frame edits: FAILURE (and an instructive one)

Real benchmark brief (pirate story P4: Noah, Emma, Sarah, Daniel around the picnic table). Full-frame insertion with position prose, then with red-rectangle target markers. Both failed the same way.

Round 4 — crop-bounded insertion: THE RECIPE THAT WORKS

Char-repair architecture with Qwen as backend: crop the target region + margin → the model inserts the person into the crop (it never sees the rest of the page) → mechanical feathered paste-back at exact coordinates. The background is pixel-immutable by construction. $0.007–0.008 per figure.

Recipe validated: plate → per-figure crop-bounded Qwen-2511 insertion (back-to-front) → mechanical feathered paste-back. Positions obeyed, poses per brief, background untouchable, ~$0.03 per 4-character page. Remaining engineering: non-overlapping crop planner (or grouped insertion for adjacent figures), identity-fidelity eval vs refs, tiny-background-figure quality check.
